name: Pura Lempuyang Luhur
significance: A hilltop sanctuary on Mount Lempuyang in eastern Bali, it is the seventh and highest of the temples in the Lempuyang complex and is counted among the island's nine holiest places of worship, revered as the guardian of the eastern direction.

name: Pura Taman Ayun
deity: Hindu gods and the ancestors of the Mengwi royal house
significance: A moated royal temple laid out in three courtyards with ranks of tiered meru towers, raised in 1634 by Gusti Agung Putu, king of Mengwi, to honour his ancestors; renovated in 1750 and again in 1937, it was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2012 as part of Bali's subak cultural landscape.

name: Pura Goa Lawah
significance: Built at the mouth of a bat-filled sea cave on the Klungkung coast and founded in the eleventh century by Mpu Kuturan, one of the priests who established Hinduism on Bali; one of its three meru towers is dedicated to Shiva, and the site became a strategic position during the 1849 War of Kusamba between the Klungkung kingdom and the Dutch colonial army.
story: The cave is held to be the domain of Naga Basuki, a primordial dragon believed to keep the balance of the cosmos.

name: Muara Takus
significance: A Mahayana Buddhist temple and stupa complex in inland Riau raised under the Srivijaya empire in the eleventh century and substantially reworked in the twelfth, serving as both a religious and a trading centre; recorded by European surveyors from 1860 and mapped by archaeologists in 1983, it is now a protected national monument.

name: Muaro Jambi Temple Compounds
significance: An extensive red-brick Buddhist temple precinct strung along the Batang Hari river, built up by the Melayu kingdom as it became Sumatra's dominant economic power in the twelfth and thirteenth centuries; the site was abandoned after a Singhasari attack in 1278 and rediscovered in 1824.

name: Arulmigu Balathandayuthapani Temple
significance: Penang's principal Murugan temple, known as the Waterfall Hilltop Temple: a shrine at the foot of the waterfall from about 1800 became the island's Thaipusam focal point, was relocated uphill after land was bought in 1914, and was rebuilt on a raised site from 2006 with a 21.6 m seven-tier gopuram, consecrated on 29 June 2012.
story: The temple's golden vel recalls the tale of the spear forged by Shiva's consort Parasakthi in eighteen forms that fused into a single indestructible weapon and was given to Murugan.

name: Nattukkottai Chettiar Temple, Penang
significance: A Murugan temple in George Town founded around 1854, after Penang's Nattukottai Chettiar community bought the land for residential quarters; its roof recesses carry hundreds of devotional paintings brought from India.

name: Sri Kandaswamy Kovil, Brickfields
significance: Founded by Kuala Lumpur's Ceylon Tamil community, which met to establish it in 1890, bought the Jalan Scott land in 1901 and held the first Maha Kumbabhishekam in February 1909; the temple maintains Saiva Siddhanta practice and was modelled on the Nallur Kandaswamy temple in Jaffna.

name: Sam Poh Tong Temple
significance: A Mahayana temple built inside a limestone cave at Ipoh, taken as a meditation hermitage in 1890 by a monk from China who lived there until his death and kept up by monks and nuns after him; the present temple buildings date from the 1950s, and the cave paintings blend Buddhist, Taoist and Hindu imagery.

name: Sri Srinivasa Perumal Temple
deity: Venkateswara (Srinivasa Perumal), a form of Vishnu
significance: One of Singapore's oldest Hindu temples, raised by early Tamil settlers on land bought in 1851 and finished in 1855; first known as Sri Narasimha Perumal Temple, it gained its five-tier gopuram in 1966 through the gift of the migrant merchant P. Govindasamy Pillai and was gazetted a national monument in 1978.

name: Sri Veeramakaliamman Temple
significance: A Little India temple to the fierce form of Kali, begun as a shrine by Bengali labourers in 1855 and built as a temple in 1881, following South Indian Tamil rather than northeastern Indian conventions; during the Japanese occupation it sheltered and fed more than twenty destitute people a night through the air raids.

name: Buddha Tooth Relic Temple and Museum
deity: Buddha (sacred tooth relic); halls to Maitreya, Guanyin, Manjushri and Samantabhadra
significance: A temple and museum complex on South Bridge Road in Chinatown, completed in 2007 to enshrine a relic venerated as a tooth of the Buddha; its abbot Ven. Shi Fa Zhao rejected nine earlier proposals before settling on a northern Chinese design drawn from Tang-dynasty Buddhist architecture, with Japanese and Tibetan touches in some rooms.

name: Sri Thendayuthapani Temple
significance: Built at Tank Road in 1859 by Singapore's Chettiar community and still run by the Chettiars' Temple Society, the Murugan temple was wholly reconstructed at a cost of S$3.3 million and reconsecrated in November 1983, renovated again in 2022, and gazetted as Singapore's 67th national monument in 2014; its Thaipusam observances draw devotees carrying kavadi and milk pots.
